title: What are the zones of the ocean?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How deep does sunlight go in the ocean?
What is the deepest part of the ocean?
How do animals live in the dark deep sea?

explain.say: The ocean is not the same all the way down. Scientists divide it into zones by how much sunlight reaches them.

faq.q: Why does most sea life live near the surface?
faq.a: Only the top 200 metres or so get enough sunlight for phytoplankton to make food by photosynthesis. They feed almost everything else, so life is richest there.

faq.q: How do animals live in the dark deep sea?
faq.a: Many make their own light, called bioluminescence, to find food or mates. They eat food that sinks from above, and near hot vents some depend on bacteria that make food from chemicals.
asks: Why do deep sea animals glow?

faq.q: What is the deepest part of the ocean?
faq.a: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, nearly 11,000 metres down. Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2 kilometres of water above its peak.
asks: How deep is the Mariana Trench?

faq.q: How much does pressure increase with depth?
faq.a: Every 10 metres of seawater adds about one more atmosphere of pressure. At the bottom of the Mariana Trench the pressure is over 1,000 times that at the surface.
asks: Why is the deep sea high pressure?

faq.q: How cold is the deep ocean?
faq.a: Below about 1,000 metres the water is usually between 0 and 4 degrees Celsius, even under tropical seas, because cold, dense water from the polar regions sinks and spreads along the bottom.
asks: Is the bottom of the sea cold?

facts: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is nearly 11,000 metres deep, the deepest known point in the ocean.
Every 10 metres of seawater adds about one atmosphere of pressure.

quiz.say: In which ocean zone do phytoplankton grow?
quiz.why: Phytoplankton need sunlight to make food, and only the top 200 metres or so get enough light.

wrong.1: The midnight zone gets no sunlight at all, so plants cannot grow there.
wrong.2: The trenches are the darkest, deepest places in the ocean, with no sunlight.
